Boundary Event

General Concept: A Boundary Event in BPMN is attached to the boundary of an activity and is triggered by an event (error, timer, message, etc.) during the activity's execution. It can interrupt or continue the activity based on its configuration.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, Boundary Events are attached to activities and can interrupt or continue the activity based on configuration. The engine manages subscriptions, variable scope, and event handling. Input mappings using FEEL expressions can be used to process event data. Supports error, timer, and message events, and can trigger alternative flows or compensation.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Boundary Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Attach to an activity and wait for a specific event (error, timer, message, etc.) during execution.
  • Configure interrupting or non-interrupting behavior for the activity.
  • Define input mappings using FEEL expressions to process event data.
  • Set up error handling and alternative flows for robust process control.
  • Monitor event handling and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for error handling, timeouts, or external signals.

 

Example: Task Timeout Handling with Timer Boundary Event

 

This example shows a process where a Timer Boundary Event is attached to a User Task to handle timeouts. If the task is not completed in time, the boundary event triggers an alternative flow. This demonstrates robust timeout handling in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use boundary events for robust error handling and timeouts.
  • Configure event type and behavior (interrupting/non-interrupting).
  • Document expected triggers and outcomes.

Pitfalls:

  • Unconfigured boundary events may not handle errors as expected.
  • Incorrect event type or mapping can block the process.
